correctness.rationale: Every automorphism is monomial because zero mixed products force at most one nonzero entry per coefficient-matrix row; invertibility forces a permutation and nonzero cycle weights force that permutation to be a rotation. Scalar recurrences classify all lifts. Rotation 0 has exactly 21 diagonal lifts, rotation 2 exactly 21, rotation 1 none; hence the quotient is C3 and the group has order 63. Every rotation-2 lift cubes on e0 as multiplication by zeta inverse, so has order 9, proving non-splitting. A unique normal C7 and a rotation lift C9 generate the full group and conjugation has order 3; group type C7 semidirect C9. Element-order spectrum follows and is checked by direct finite-field enumeration for q=43,211,337. The all-prime-power proof is independent of those finite checks.

originality.rationale: The result is not the known generic monomial-orbit principle or existence of non-split automorphism extensions. It supplies the exact nonabelian order-63 group C7 semidirect C9, diagonal C21, quotient C3, and an unavoidable order-nine lift, on a single directed weighted six-cycle for an infinite finite-field family. A fully inspected 2026 related construction has group C9 instead, and the 2023 general classification only supplies monomial orbits, not the particular extension and arithmetic obstruction. Claims and implications of the most relevant accessible prior sources and own recoverable claims were compared. Residual priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The natural exact sequence of diagonal and permutation automorphisms is a recognized structural invariant. This infinite arithmetic family exhibits explicit nonabelian, nonsplit order-63 groups with one weighted directed cycle, unlike generic realization theorems and the published abelian C9 non-split six-dimensional example. The explicit diagonal kernel, rotation image, cube obstruction, group type and order spectrum give a complete and motivated classification for the displayed family; the identical support graph with unit weights has a different rotation image. Question 33 of the 2026 evolution-algebra survey identifies splitting classification as a mathematically motivated gap.
